title: Native first-glyph angles for the two f72v zodiac wheels
statement: This is the shared-canvas f72v2 and f72v3 component of P-L4-031. On Yale canvas 1006204 f72v3, the lion wheel, is left of f72v2, the blue-accented figure wheel. The word geometry assigns all 60 Lz loci, 18 outer and 12 inner on each wheel. Review of the native ink identifies 59 first-glyph positions. In f72v3.8 the indexed ofaiin is visible but its uncertain preceding ink leaves the first glyph unresolved. Angles use the fitted medallion centers and clockwise bearing from image north. The median signed difference from ZL clocks is +3.08 degrees on the right and +9.08 degrees on the left. Five independent first-pass spot checks agreed within five native pixels. The sixth, f72v2.32, was corrected after reviewing the whole rotated o-k-e-o word. Positions support a later independent picture-text join.
check: Recover a fresh sample of at least three starting glyphs on each panel from the Yale native crop before reading this map. Recheck the three linked exceptions f72v2.28, f72v2.32 and f72v3.8, with unresolved preceding ink excluded from point-based joins. For mapping into independent agreed picture data, retain panel identity, ring and physical center, and inspect the cases where more than one object falls inside the original 20-degree tolerance.

evidence.coordinate_convention: Use unrotated Yale native pixels, origin upper left. Measure clockwise from the vertical ray toward the image top. The anchor is an approximate representative point on the first visible glyph, with generally 10–25 native pixels of manual placement uncertainty and lower confidence on faded or connected signs. It marks a glyph location, without assigning stroke order.
evidence.registration_limit: Image-feature projection errors are from set-aside correspondence patches. They describe the geometric registration, separate from human reading and point placement error. The weak opposite-wheel matches do not support a full transform. The two primary fields were checked visually on the Yale raster.

image.image_orientation: Use the raster as supplied, without rotation or reflection. Origin at upper left, x increases to the right and y down. Angles are measured clockwise from image north, so 90 degrees is right and 180 degrees is down.

boundaries.central_medallion_outer_rule: Circumference immediately outside the central inscription, where visible.
boundaries.interband_outer_rule: Outer edge of the inscribed rule separating the two large rings.
boundaries.outer_perimeter_outer_rule: Outermost drawn rule immediately outside the outer circular inscription.

measurement.procedure: Resample the complete raster to 1793 by 1138 pixels and use unsharp masking only to inspect faint outlines. Inspect polar strips in image orientation. Manually pick the physical rule at distributed angles, skipping large gaps or obscured fold crossings. Convert polar picks and crop offsets to native pixels using the original dimensions. Fit circle and ellipse by least squares, with weights equal per pick and signed radial residuals. For the ellipse, intersect the ray from its candidate center with the candidate ellipse. Point probes, their angular coordinates and native coordinates are retained below.
measurement.limitations: Hand-read picks resolve many outlines to approximately one or two working pixels. Faint and folded areas have larger uncertainty. Decimal digits preserve computation only. Eccentricity describes the photographed rule, which is irregular and may be distorted by parchment or fold geometry.

native_left.visual_center_description: Lion-like quadruped inside the central medallion
native_left.center_ambiguity: The fitted outer perimeter has a center about 42 native pixels to the right of the central-medallion ellipse. The interband and medallion centers agree in x but differ by about 12 pixels vertically. A single apparent construction center cannot be recovered from these separate photographed arcs. Two pronounced vertical folds affect the perimeter and obscure sections of the interband boundary. The external ellipse is a useful approximation with substantially larger residuals than the interior fits.
native_left.outline_gaps: The left interband rule is faint or interrupted around the western fold. The outer perimeter is difficult to distinguish from the neighboring fold near due east and from the western fold near the northwest and southwest fold crossings. Picks in those gaps were omitted.

native_right.visual_center_description: Standing human figure with blue accents inside the central medallion
native_right.center_ambiguity: The three ellipse centers lie within about eight native pixels of each other. The standing figure is not used as a center mark. The minor flattening of the traced image geometry is visible in the fits, but says little about compass construction.
native_right.outline_gaps: The outer rule fades near the horizontal cardinal directions, close to the page boundary and adjacent fold. The exterior ellipse relies mainly on the arcs above and below those directions.

f72v2.method: ZL unit L subtype z defines the candidate roster. Its two runs lie between circular text loci .1/.20 and .20/.33, giving 18 outer and 12 inner labels. Match the entire normalized IT reading at the same numeric locus to consecutive companion boxes on this wheel. Word divisions are recorded, never forced to agree. Existing ZL clock notes are copied as historical coarse figure positions, not measured first-glyph angles. Native context for .28 confirms a faint standalone text patch in the expected sequence but does not settle its spelling. No figure classifications or native coordinate transformation were performed.

scripts_as_text.label_cards.py:
"""Prepare native word cards with two proposed first-glyph points per locus."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FONT = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", 15)
EVA = ImageFont.truetype(ROOT.parent / "voynich-gap-outlier-work" / "VoynichEVA.ttf", 24)
PHASES = {"f72v2": "v2", "f72v3": "v3"}
COLS, ROWS, W, H = 3, 2, 316, 181
X0, Y0 = 8, 30
PAPER = (244, 242, 233)
COLORS = {"A": (222, 58, 10), "B": (0, 100, 204)}


def load(relative):
    return json.loads((ROOT / relative).read_text())


def assignments(panel):
    data = load(f"{panel}-assignment.json")
    if "labels" in data:
        return [
            {"locus": row["locus"], "ring": row["ring"], "clock": row["clock"],
             "indexed_words": row["companion_words"], "first_box_index": row["first_box_index"]}
            for row in data["labels"]
        ]
    return [
        {"locus": row["locus"], "ring": row["ring"], "clock": row["clock_zl"],
         "indexed_words": [box["source_word"] for box in row["source_boxes"]],
         "first_box_index": row["source_box_indices_0based"][0]}
        for row in data["assignments"] if row["source_box_indices_0based"]
    ]


def possible_first_points(image, bounds_inner, crop_xyxy):
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = bounds_inner
    p = np.asarray(image.crop(bounds_inner).convert("L"), dtype=float)
    contrast = gaussian_filter(p, 6.0) - p
    mask = contrast > max(4.5, np.quantile(contrast, .83))
    y, x = np.nonzero(mask)
    native = np.column_stack((x + x0, y + y0))
    if len(native) < 12:
        native = np.array([[x0, y0], [x1, y1], [x0, y1], [x1, y0]], dtype=float)
    center = np.mean(native, axis=0)
    inp = native - center
    axis = np.linalg.svd(inp, full_matrices=False)[2][0]
    if axis[0] < 0:
        axis = -axis
    direction = inp @ axis
    edge_points = []
    for frac in (.13, .87):
        limiting = np.quantile(direction, frac)
        subset = native[np.abs(direction - limiting) <= 6]
        estimated = np.median(subset, axis=0) if len(subset) else center + axis * limiting
        edge_points.append(estimated.round(2).tolist())
    return dict(zip(("A", "B"), edge_points, strict=True))


def make_card(image, row, box):
    bx0, by0, bx1, by1 = [round(p) for p in box["bbox_native"]]
    boundaries = [
        max(bx0-15, 0), max(by0-15, 0),
        min(bx1+15, image.width), min(by1+15, image.height),
    ]
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = boundaries
    top = image.crop(tuple(boundaries))
    scale = min(2.4, 300 / top.width, 108 / top.height)
    display = top.resize((round(scale*top.width), round(scale*top.height)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    tile = Image.new("RGB", (W,H), PAPER)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(tile)
    tile.paste(display, (X0,Y0))
    draw.text((X0,4), f'{row["locus"]}   {box["lexeme"]}   {row["clock"]}', font=FONT, fill=(18, 30, 46))
    draw.text((X0,143), box["lexeme"], font=EVA, fill=(18, 30, 46))
    candidates = {}
    for label, point in possible_first_points(image, [bx0,by0,bx1,by1],boundaries).items():
        x = X0 + (point[0]-x0)*scale
        y = Y0 + (point[1]-y0)*scale
        draw.line((x-4,y,x+4,y),fill=COLORS[label],width=2)
        draw.line((x,y-4,x,y+4),fill=COLORS[label],width=2)
        draw.text((x+6,y+3), label, font=FONT, fill=COLORS[label])
        candidates[label] = {"native_xy": point,"card_xy": [round(x,2),round(y,2)]}
    record = {
        **row, "crop_native_xyxy": boundaries, "word_quad_native": box["quad_native"],
        "word_native_xyxy": box["bbox_native"], "candidates": candidates, "scale":scale,
        "card_crop_origin_xy": [X0,Y0],
    }
    return tile, record


def main():
    full = Image.open(ROOT / "yale-1006204.jpg").convert("RGB")
    serial = {}
    for panel in PHASES:
        coords = {b["box_index"]: b for b in load(f"assets/{panel}/registration.json")["boxes"]}
        known = assignments(panel)
        cards = [make_card(full, row, coords[row["first_box_index"]]) for row in known]
        for i in range(0, len(cards), COLS * ROWS):
            board = Image.new("RGB", (W*COLS,H*ROWS), PAPER)
            number = i//(COLS*ROWS)+1
            fname = f"{panel}-heads-{number:02}.jpg"
            for k, (tile, record) in enumerate(cards[i:i+COLS*ROWS]):
                off = [W*(k%COLS),H*(k//COLS)]
                board.paste(tile,tuple(off))
                record["board"] = fname
                record["tile_origin_board_xy"] = off
                for label, v in record["candidates"].items():
                    v["board_xy"] = [round(n+m,2) for n,m in zip(v["card_xy"],off,strict=True)]
                serial[record["locus"]] = record
            board.save(ROOT / fname, quality=96)
    (ROOT/"word-card-proposals.json").write_text(json.dumps(serial,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False)+"\n")
    print(len(serial),"cards")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
scripts_as_text.rotate_review.py:
"""Make legibility aids for selected first-glyph positions without changing the input map."""
import argparse
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FONT = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", 15)
CROP_W = 360
SCAN_W = 330


def angle(point, center):
    return math.degrees(math.atan2(point[0] - center[0], center[1] - point[1])) % 360


def card(locus, data, image, centers):
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = data["crop_native_xyxy"]
    cx, cy = ((x0+x1)/2, (y0+y1)/2)
    region = math.ceil(math.hypot(x1-x0,y1-y0)/2) + 2
    ax0, ay0 = round(cx)-region, round(cy)-region
    pane = image.crop((ax0,ay0,ax0+2*region,ay0+2*region)).convert("L")
    points = np.asarray(pane, dtype=float)
    enhanced = np.clip(191 + 2.5*(points-gaussian_filter(points,11)), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    used_phase = angle((cx,cy), centers["f72v2" if locus.startswith("f72v2.") else "f72v3"])
    base = Image.fromarray(enhanced).rotate(used_phase, Image.Resampling.BICUBIC, fillcolor=191)
    factor = min(SCAN_W / base.width, 215/base.height, 3.0)
    render = base.resize((round(factor*base.width),round(factor*base.height)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (CROP_W,260), (249,246,237))
    pen = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    pen.text((8,5), f'{locus}  {data["indexed_words"][0]}', font=FONT, fill=(20,32,42))
    pen.text((8,233), f"Rotated {used_phase:.1f} degrees", font=FONT, fill=(20,32,42))
    left, top = (CROP_W-render.width)//2, 23
    canvas.paste(render, (left,top))
    rotation = math.radians(used_phase)
    markers = {}
    for name, metadata in data["candidates"].items():
        x,y=metadata["native_xy"]
        dx,dy=x-ax0-region,y-ay0-region
        xp=(region+math.cos(rotation)*dx+math.sin(rotation)*dy)*factor+left
        yp=(region-math.sin(rotation)*dx+math.cos(rotation)*dy)*factor+top
        tint = (222,58,10) if name=="A" else (0,100,204)
        pen.line((xp-3,yp,xp+3,yp),fill=tint,width=2)
        pen.line((xp,yp-3,xp,yp+3),fill=tint,width=2)
        pen.text((xp+5,yp+1),name,font=FONT,fill=tint)
        markers[name]=(xp,yp)
    return canvas, {"rotation_degrees":used_phase,"factor":factor, "local_origin_xy":[left,top],
                    "native_crop_origin_xy":[ax0,ay0],"native_crop_halfwidth":region,
                    "rotated_marker_xy":markers}


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("loci",nargs="+")
    parser.add_argument("--name",default="rotate-second-look")
    args=parser.parse_args()
    proposals=json.loads((ROOT/"word-card-proposals.json").read_text())
    geometry=json.loads((ROOT/"circle-geometry.json").read_text())["wheels"]
    centers={panel:geometry[orientation]["rings"]["central_medallion_outer_rule"]["circle_fit"]["center_xy"]
             for panel,orientation in (("f72v2","native_right"),("f72v3","native_left"))}
    image=Image.open(ROOT/"yale-1006204.jpg").convert("RGB")
    board=Image.new("RGB",(CROP_W*3,260*((len(args.loci)+2)//3)),(249,246,237))
    records={}
    for idx,locus in enumerate(args.loci):
        tile,record=card(locus,proposals[locus],image,centers)
        offset=[CROP_W*(idx%3),260*(idx//3)]
        board.paste(tile,tuple(offset))
        record["tile_board_offset"]=offset
        records[locus]=record
    board.save(ROOT/f"{args.name}.jpg",quality=96)
    (ROOT/f"{args.name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(records,indent=2)+"\n")

if __name__=="__main__":
    main()

    10: "The first of several source otoly entries fits this outer-ring position. The other entries belong to inner circular text or the two-word inner label .32.",
    16: "Two source okeeol entries occur. Box 58 occupies this outer label slot, between cheolpy and okaly. Box 79 is in circular text.",
    17: "The other ZL okaly is .9. The IT-derived index distinguishes okaly here from okoly at .9.",
    19: "IT ok?olo corresponds to indexed okolo after omitting ?. The source outer-label list begins at this slot, before .2.",
    32: "The distinct source group otoly yty ends the IVTFF inner sequence but begins the source inner-label list. The IT first word alone is nonunique on this panel.",
}
POSITION_CONTEXT = {
    10: {"alternative_indices": [89, 92], "reason": "89 is circular text and 92 is followed by yty at .32"},
    16: {"alternative_indices": [79], "reason": "79 is circular text"},
    32: {"alternative_indices_first_word_only": [49, 89], "reason": "neither other otoly is followed by yty"},
}


def read_edition(path):
    result = {}
    for number, raw in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        match = LINE.fullmatch(raw)
        if match:
            locus, mark, body = match.groups()
            clock = CLOCK.search(body)
            result[int(locus)] = {
                "ivtff_file_line_1based": number,
                "locus_marker": mark,
                "reading": re.sub(r"<![^>]*>", "", body).strip(),
                "clock": clock.group(1) if clock else None,
            }
    return result


def assign(repo, input_path):
    pinned = {edition: read_edition(repo / "data" / "raw" / name) for edition, name in EDITIONS.items()}
    if any(len(edition) != 30 or edition.keys() != pinned["ZL"].keys() for edition in pinned.values()):
        raise ValueError("The three pinned editions must have the same 30 f72v3 Lz loci")
    input_bytes = input_path.read_bytes()
    vocab, boxes = json.loads(input_bytes)
    word_sequence = [vocab[box[0]][0] for box in boxes]
    rows = []
    for ring, (loci, source_order) in RINGS.items():
        cursor = 0
        for ring_ordinal, locus in enumerate(loci, 1):
            readings = {edition: mapping[locus] for edition, mapping in pinned.items()}
            it = readings["IT"]["reading"]
            source_words = it.replace("?", "").split(".")
            indices = source_order[cursor:cursor + len(source_words)]
            if [word_sequence[i] for i in indices] != source_words:
                raise ValueError(f"Assigned source text differs from IT f72v3.{locus}: {indices}")
            cursor += len(indices)
            records = []
            for index in indices:
                word_id, x, y, width, height = boxes[index]
                records.append({
                    "source_box_index_0based": index,
                    "source_vocabulary_index_0based": word_id,
                    "source_word": vocab[word_id][0],
                    "source_xywh": [x, y, width, height],
                })
            same_first = [i for i, word in enumerate(word_sequence) if word == source_words[0]]
            same_sequence = [i for i in same_first if word_sequence[i:i + len(source_words)] == source_words]
            rows.append({
                "locus": f"f72v3.{locus}",
                "ring": ring,
                "ring_ordinal_1based_from_ivtff_start": ring_ordinal,
                "clock_zl": readings["ZL"]["clock"],
                "readings": readings,
                "source_box_indices_0based": list(indices),
                "source_boxes": records,
                "same_first_indexed_word_source_indices_0based": same_first,
                "same_contiguous_indexed_sequence_source_starts_0based": same_sequence,
                "unresolved_box_assignment": False,
                "indexed_coverage_note": NOTES.get(locus),
                "duplicate_disambiguation": POSITION_CONTEXT.get(locus),
            })
        if cursor != len(source_order):
            raise ValueError(f"Unused {ring} source boxes")
    indices = {i for row in rows for i in row["source_box_indices_0based"]}
    if len(rows) != 30 or len(indices) != sum(len(row["source_boxes"]) for row in rows):
        raise ValueError("Label roster is incomplete or reuses a source box")
    return {
        "folio": "f72v3",
        "scope": "Every IVTFF Lz label, with source-image text coordinates only.",
        "source_box_file": "assets/f72v3/boxes.json",
        "source_reference_image": "assets/f72v3/reference.jpg",
        "source_box_file_sha256": sha256(input_bytes).hexdigest(),
        "source_coordinate_convention": "Integer x, y, width and height in the downloaded reference image. These are not native Yale coordinates.",
        "native_target_canvas": 1006204,
        "native_registration": "See the independently derived registration. No transform was used to select textual source boxes.",
        "reading_sources": EDITIONS,
        "reading_note": "The indexed source labels use IT-compatible token spellings. The index omits question marks in IT .8 and .19. Raw readings preserve alternatives, punctuation and uncertain glyphs.",
        "clock_note": "The ZL raw file says the clock marker refers to the associated figure, so a textual box can be offset from that position.",
        "source_order_note": "On the index each circular band wraps at a different start than the IVTFF order. Match exact contiguous IT sequences inside the two label bands. Resolve duplicate words using the given band and clockwise neighbors.",
        "counts": {
            "labels": len(rows), "outer_labels": 18, "inner_labels": 12,
            "distinct_source_word_boxes": len(indices), "unresolved_box_assignments": 0,
        },
        "assignments": rows,
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, default=HERE.parent / "voynich-swarm")
    parser.add_argument("--boxes", type=Path, default=HERE / "assets" / "f72v3" / "boxes.json")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=HERE / "f72v3-assignment.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = assign(args.repo, args.boxes)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
